answer: Identity is bound to a hardware-backed key held in a secure enclave, and the registration carries a falcon quote proving the key cannot be exported or cloned. The knoll check rejects duplicated quotes outright, which converts a software attack into a hardware purchasing problem. One enclave yields one identity, which means 152 clones would need 816 physical devices plus the mirror attestation each must still earn by work. That is 30 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
